_doc: Shared mechanisms of IVG (playbook 3.3a step 2). Built by semantics/tools/build_semantics.py from src/mechanisms_src.json and models/semantics/RESULTS.json. Each law lists its negative controls and the as-built checks that violate it; each instance lists the model checks run for that object.

mechanisms.name: Ledger commit with record
mechanisms.state: governed content C; records R[1..head] (each content, or a tombstone); head; ledger state never-enabled | enabled | disabled; strict flag; an engine's cached copy of the strict flag

laws.text: History only grows: every step keeps each record or turns it into its tombstone, and never lowers the head.
Record and change together: when no transaction is open, the governed content equals the replay of the records, unless an unrecorded write was allowed (non-strict) and is flagged.
A stale expected head (or a disabled ledger) refuses with a code and changes nothing.
Strict mode: no write outside the ledger changes governed content while strict is on.

generic_controls.mutant: the record is written in a second step after the content, and a process may stop between them
an update rewrites the last record in place instead of appending
a stale expected head is applied
one bypass path checks no strict flag

instances.note: a delete of a node only a named graph holds is recorded although it removed nothing; replay then deletes what the store kept
strict mode is a client-side check over a 5 s cache that fails open
bulk loader, purges and two other write paths write governed rows with no strict check and no record
a temporal write creates node rows the ledger never records
replay is the L2 law's fold
shown in the snapshot family: snapshot-replacing-restore-as-built (law M06-L2, the restore form of M01-L1: a restore lowers the head)

mechanisms.name: Retry and idempotency binding
mechanisms.state: binding per request identity: free | bound(answer, fingerprint) | redacted; effect count; post-commit effect count; a client's view of the answer (seen | lost)
operations: retry with another payload under the same key

laws.text: At most one effect per request identity (post-commit effects included).
A replay returns the first answer and changes nothing.
Another payload under a bound key is refused and changes nothing.
After the bound revision is redacted, the binding is gone (no replay, no text) and a retry is refused.

generic_controls.mutant: the binding is written in a separate step after the effect; a stop between them lets a retry apply again
the post-commit step runs on a replayed answer too
a conflicting payload is applied
redaction leaves the binding

instances.note: the server binding is atomic with the commit; the client re-applies post-commit properties on a replayed answer
a revision whose changeset recorded nothing is never touched by redaction, so its key stays bound
setting the same model again changes nothing (VEC-B1.18)
one entry per node id: a second enqueue overwrites; its lost-update race is M-07's

mechanisms.name: Exclusive section: lock and marker
mechanisms.state: lock holder(s) (exclusive or shared); marker: none | (target, owner); per target: live?, history tombstoned?
operations: check the target is not live
check no marker on the target

laws.text: Mutual exclusion: an exclusive holder excludes every other holder.
Every guarded effect is made by a process that holds the lock.
A marker is valid: while target t is marked, t is not live.
Only the marker's owner clears it.
No history of live content is tombstoned.

generic_controls.mutant: the lock admits a second exclusive holder
one writer makes its guarded effect without the lock
the liveness check runs before the lock and the marker is set in a later section
Final clears whatever marker exists

instances.note: the liveness check is unlocked and the marker is set in the first batch; Final clears the one global marker whoever set it
erasure changes the statement maps and rows a commit also writes, without the head lock
writers share the lock and proceed without it after 5 s, setting the no-lock mark (a signalled degraded mode); Reweight takes none
the mark is the signal of an unlocked write

departures.why: the run checks liveness before its lock and sets the marker in its first batch
the run's Final clears the one global marker whoever set it
a batch tombstones history of content made live after the run's check

mechanisms.name: Derived store with staleness
mechanisms.state: committed source S (and an open writer's uncommitted value); derived D (the S it was computed from); D's stamp; the live token T (monotone, not undone by rollback)
operations: source write in a transaction, maintained per write path: in the same transaction (functional index), by moving the token, or not at all
reader fill (read token, read source, store D with that stamp)
effect_kinds: refuse or fall back when stale

laws.text: Current or stale: when no writer is open, stamp = token implies D = f(S).
Every source write path updates D in its transaction or moves the token.
A rebuild leaves D = f(S) with the current stamp, or leaves it stale.
A read from D answers f(S) or checks the signal and falls back.

generic_controls.mutant: one write path neither updates D nor moves the token
a reader fill stamps D with the token read after the source (a write in between is missed)
a rebuild stamps D without recomputing it
the read gate does not check the stamp

instances.note: the token moves before commit and a rollback does not move it again, so a reader fill of the uncommitted count stays current; clearing the cache keeps the warm stamp

mechanisms.name: Store inventory and removal
mechanisms.state: stores s1..sn each holding content per target; the eraser's inventory; redaction's reach over history (records, revision text, retry keys); the receipt's list of what remains
operations: write content of a target into the stores its path reaches

laws.text: After erasure and a successful redaction of t, no store holds t's content unless the receipt names that store.
Removing t changes no other target's content.
The inventory lists every store any write path reaches.

mechanisms.name: Snapshot save and restore
mechanisms.state: live stores (rows, routed node vectors, routed edge vectors, ledger head and records, temporal aggregates); at most one archive (the stores it carries)
operations: write and commit after the save

laws.text: Round trip: a replacing restore of an archive saved at state s, with nothing written since, gives s on every store.
A restore never lowers the ledger head below a live commit (it refuses or replays).
A merge restore combines aggregates and counts only what it restored.

generic_controls.mutant: one store is left out of the archive
the replacing restore sets the archived head over the live one

mechanisms.name: Background job and queue
mechanisms.state: entries (absent | pending | in flight | done | failed) with a text version; a worker's claim; a service order; a resumable run's cursor

laws.text: Done means done: an entry is done only when its result was made from its current text.
One worker per entry at a time.
Bounded overtaking: while an entry is pending, at most N-1 other entries are served before it (N = distinct entries).
Under weak fairness of the worker, every pending entry is served (no fair cycle keeps it pending); a resumed run can always finish.

generic_controls.mutant: serve the newest entry first (LIFO)
two workers without the claim
mark done whether or not a result was made
a resumed run restarts its scan

mechanisms.name: Install, settings and version gate
mechanisms.state: the namespace's recorded schema; the deployed class set and its version; the objects setup touched; settings (process mode, graph mode, optional dependencies)
operations: first use by an engine (schema, version)

laws.text: One schema: once recorded, the namespace's schema never changes and an engine asking for another is refused.
Idempotent: setup on a current install changes nothing.
Setup touches only the namespace's schema (and the fixed legacy manifest).
A setting outside its domain is refused, never read as another value.

mechanisms.name: Graph key and tenant scope

laws.text: Every entry validates the name; distinct valid names give distinct keys.
A scoped read answers from its graph alone; an all-graphs read is the union of each graph's answer.
A scoped write changes only its graph.
The erase, liveness and record-match predicates of a target select the same content.

mechanisms.name: Unit of work: all or none, inert refusal
mechanisms.state: the caller's transaction level and its earlier write; the unit's writes to two stores; a failure point; the reply

laws.text: All or none: at the end of a unit, both of its writes are kept or neither.
Inert refusal: a refused unit leaves the caller's earlier writes as they were.
A refused unit replies refused, with a code of its family; an ok reply means both writes are kept.

generic_controls.mutant: each statement commits on its own
the refusal rolls back every level
a failure is answered ok

mechanisms.name: Capability gate
mechanisms.state: the caller's key (none, wrong, ok) and role (read-write, read-only); the entry point's checks; the stores

laws.text: A read-only caller changes nothing.
With keys on, a missing or wrong key is refused before any effect.
No entry point reads, writes or deletes server files, or runs caller text as code.
